summary: 1928 Aermotor steel fire tower in Harriman State Park; restored by volunteers in 2018, then fenced off and closed by November 2021 with no reopening found.

facts.design: 60-foot Aermotor LS-40 steel tower with a 7-by-7-foot metal cab and windows of an unusual design

access.note: Fenced off and closed by November 2021; the 2023 chapter report lists it as closed pending engineering inspection. No reopening found.

visit.trail_note: Closed and fenced off in the latest sources; no reopening date found

events.note: Constructed by the Palisades Interstate Park Commission, which operated it until 1931
Operation passed to Forest Fire Control; the register says it closed in the 1970s
Observer on duty nine hours a day, April to November, per a 1932 Journal-News item quoted by Forest Lookouts
Registered April 28, 1997 as US 213, NY 16; nominated by Lawrence G. Paul
Closed by January 2018, with the bottom set of stairs removed
Stairs, platforms, cab floor and windows replaced and tower painted over April and June 2018 weekends
April 2021 chapter newsletter: many cab windows missing and a great deal of graffiti
Fenced off and closed by November 2021, perhaps permanently

corrections.why: The earliest closure report I found is the register's visit note of January 21, 2018, which says the tower is closed. I found no April 2017 report.
Hike the Hudson Valley's November 2021 note already reports the tower fenced off and closed; the 2023 chapter report says it is still closed.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Team Rubicon describes 50 of its team members doing the work. Hike the Hudson Valley credits the New York chapter and Team Rubicon. An August 2018 visitor did not know who did the work. The story names the crews the sources describe and notes the visitor's uncertainty.
The register gives 1,260 ft (384 m); the 1932 item quoted by Forest Lookouts says 1,300 feet above sea level. The story gives no elevation.

notes_for_editor: Brief's April 2017 closure and 2022 closure are not supported: earliest closure found is the NHLR visit of January 21, 2018; fenced off by November 2021 per Hike the Hudson Valley. Brief's 'finished 3 June' (2018) and the May 21, 2021 paint-over were not found in sources read and are omitted. A Facebook and a Reddit search snippet mention a later volunteer effort to reopen the tower, but those pages were not read, so nothing from them is used. 'Today' status rests on the 2023 chapter report and a 2021 note; a fresh check is advisable. The 1932 newspaper item is seen only as quoted on Forest Lookouts. The brief's 'Gate Hill' name for the tower is not in any source read beyond that 1932 item. Photos not added.
